Generated from the TypeScript sources by TypeDoc. Each sensor also has a focused reference with just its own symbols: [SR04](sr04/api.md) · [VL53L4CD](vl53l4cd/api.md) · [VL53L8CX](vl53l8cx/api.md) · [VL53L8CH](vl53l8ch/api.md) · [TMF8829](tmf8829/api.md) · [VL53L5CX](vl53l5cx/api.md) · [VL53L7CX](vl53l7cx/api.md) · [VL53L7CH](vl53l7ch/api.md) · [VL53L0X](vl53l0x/api.md) · [VL53L1CX](vl53l1cx/api.md) · [VL53L1CB](vl53l1cb/api.md) · [VL53L3CX](vl53l3cx/api.md) · [VL53L4CX](vl53l4cx/api.md) · [BNO086](bno086/api.md) · [BNO055](bno055/api.md). For the narrative guides see the per-sensor `docs/<sensor>/` pages and `docs/overview.md`.

# Class: Bno055

Defined in: [sensors/bno055/bno055.ts:198](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/bno055/bno055.ts#L198)

BNO055 absolute-orientation IMU.

Typical use: `configure()` (CONFIG → units → axis remap → optional
calibration profile → NDOF), then `startStream(10)` and read the `samples`
stream, or poll `readSample()`. Streaming is timer-driven: the
data-ready interrupt does not exist on the sensor firmware these boards
carry (03.11).

Multi-step register sequences (page switches, CONFIG round trips) are
serialised internally, so concurrent calls cannot interleave mid-sequence.
Page 1 is refused while a stream runs.

The streamed samples (contract 07 §3): `on(cb)` subscribes,
`subscribe(maxsize)` iterates, `next(timeoutMs)` waits for one;
`droppedCounts` and `parseErrors` (stream reports that did not decode — a
short block) are its counters.

# Class: Bno086

Defined in: [sensors/bno086/bno086.ts:156](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/bno086/bno086.ts#L156)

BNO086 device: enable SH-2 sensors, stream typed reports.

Typical use:

    const imu = await openOnTransport(transport);   // or openDeviceFrom(...)
    if (!(imu instanceof Bno086)) throw new Error("not a BNO086");
    await imu.enable(SensorId.RotationVector, 100);
    for await (const r of imu.reports.subscribe(64)) { ... }

Callbacks run on the read-pump context — never await blocking device
methods (enable/tare/...) from inside one.

- [`DepzDevice`](#class-depzdevice)

### hardwareReset()

```ts
hardwareReset(timeoutMs?): Promise<void>;
```

Defined in: [sensors/bno086/bno086.ts:467](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/bno086/bno086.ts#L467)

Hard-reset the sensor via nRST (0x32). All SHTP state (seq counters,
partial cargos) and cached features restart from zero.

The hub's RPT_STATUS OK ack for the 0x32 command is treated as the reset
confirmation. The SH-2 executable-channel reset-complete (which the BNO08X
SH-2 spec would emit) is only waited for best-effort: older firmware
(≤ v0.95) did **not** emit it (ERRATA E9, now fixed
in newer firmware); the best-effort wait handles both, so its absence is
*not* an error — the sensor is fully usable without it.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default value |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `2000` |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`void`\>

### sleep()

```ts
sleep(): Promise<void>;
```

Defined in: [sensors/bno086/bno086.ts:515](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/bno086/bno086.ts#L515)

Put the hub to sleep: SH-2 "Sleep" (0x03 on SHTP channel 1).

Every report stops, except those enabled with
`flags: FeatureFlag.Wakeup | FeatureFlag.AlwaysOn`, which keep their rate;
the configuration (enabled sensors, rates) is kept. The hub sends no
response. [powerOn](#poweron) ends it.

On a DEPZ BNO086 (SH-2 3.12.6, 2026-10-16): all reports stopped within one
sample; a Wakeup|AlwaysOn report kept streaming at full rate on channel 4.

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`void`\>

***

```ts
powerOn(): Promise<void>;
```

End [sleep](#sleep): SH-2 "On" (0x02 on SHTP channel 1).

Every report that was enabled comes back at its rate — no need to
re-enable. The hub sends no response. Not to be confused with
[wake](#wake), which pulses the WAKE pin (board command 0x33) instead of
sending an SH-2 command.

`Promise`\<`void`\>

Set the runtime reorientation quaternion (Q14 on the wire; all zeros
clears). No response per SH-2.

The rotation is applied on the board's side (new = report * r) and is
given in the hub's own axes: x and y swapped and z negated relative to
the axes of the reports — a rotation about x here turns the reports
about y (bench, 2026-10-22, SH-2 3.12.6). The System Orientation record
(FRS 0x2D3E) uses the same axes and is read only when the hub starts.

`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

not capture any frames.

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `targetObject` | `object` |
| `constructorOpt?` | `Function` |

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

[`DepzError`](#class-depzerror).[`captureStackTrace`](#capturestacktrace-3)

## Properties

### stackTraceLimit

```ts
static stackTraceLimit: number;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `targetObject` | `object` |
| `constructorOpt?` | `Function` |

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

```ts
Error.captureStackTrace
```

# Class: DatasetPlayer

Defined in: [dataset.ts:538](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/dataset.ts#L538)

Timeline player: paced delivery with play / pause / seek / speed — the
engine behind the viewer's playback mode (contract 09 §Player; reference:
Python `DatasetPlayer`).

Timing: a media clock anchored to the host clock. Record i is due at
`anchorWall + (t_i − anchorT) / speed`; the anchor is (now, t of the last
delivered record — of the first record when none was) at play / resume /
seek, so the first record goes out at once and every later one after its
gap to the previous one. Pacing is against the clock, not cumulative: a
slow consumer gets overdue records back to back and playback does not
drift.

Records and the `done` state are delivered from timers, never inside
`play` / `seekUs` / a speed change; state changes made by those calls are
reported before they return. A record or state callback that throws is
logged (`console.error`), counted in [DatasetPlayer.callbackErrors](#callbackerrors)
and dropped: the other callbacks still get the record and playback goes on.

### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `targetObject` | `object` |
| `constructorOpt?` | `Function` |

`void`

# Class: FrameReassembler

Defined in: [protocol/vl53l8.ts:108](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/protocol/vl53l8.ts#L108)

Rebuilds full sensor frames from chunked RPT_VL53_FRAME reports.

Rules (contract 04 §4): reset on offset==0; chunks must be contiguous —
a gap discards the frame in progress; a frame completes when the
accumulated bytes equal `fullSize`. A chunk out of the rule-4 bounds
(more than `chunkMax` bytes, `fullSize` over STREAM_TOTAL_MAX, or running
past `fullSize`) is damaged: dropped and counted as a lost frame like the
other damaged input, never thrown. `chunkMax` is the device's
VL53_STREAM_FRAME_MAX (contract 11 §3: 1536 on the I2C board).

## Constructors

```ts
new FrameReassembler(chunkMax?): FrameReassembler;
```

# Class: LoopbackTransport

Defined in: [transport/loopback.ts:5](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/transport/loopback.ts#L5)

How the SDK calls a transport (contract 07 §3, "The host-supplied link") —
what a transport given to `openOnTransport` or a device constructor has to
cope with. Everything runs on the event loop: there are no threads and no
read slices.

- `open` is called once, on a transport not yet open; `readable` once, after
  it, and that iterator is the only reader for the whole connection.
- `write` is called once per frame, a whole frame per call, in frame order
  and **without waiting for the previous `write`**: unlike the other SDKs,
  this one does not serialize writes, so a transport keeps them in order
  itself. It resolves when everything is written and rejects otherwise, and
  it must settle within a bounded time: a request waits for its `write`, so
  one that never settles never ends, not even at its timeout.
- `close` is called by every `DepzDevice.close()` and when the read fails
  (then again by the program's own `close()`): it must be idempotent. It
  may come during a pending read or `write`, and it must end the `readable`
  iterator; the device does not wait for that iterator.
- `onDisconnect` is subscribed once, when the read starts.
- A loss, unless the program is closing the device: `readable` throwing
  (logged with `console.error`, kept as the `cause`; the SDK closes the
  transport), `readable` ending, or the `onDisconnect` callback (no cause;
  the SDK does not call `close` until the program does). The device closes
  and every later request fails with `DeviceLostError`.
- A rejected `write` fails only that request, as a `DepzError` as it is and
  as `DeviceLostError` otherwise (`LinkClosedError` while closing), the
  rejection as its `cause`; the device ends when the read reports the loss.
- A rejected `close` reaches the program from its own `close()` (the device
  still ends); after a failed read it is dropped.

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

generated stack trace.

details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js

  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;

  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}
```

# Class: ReplayTransport

Defined in: [transport/replay.ts:166](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/transport/replay.ts#L166)

Replays the `rx` side of a `.depzrec` capture **causally**: an rx event
is released only after the host has written at least as many tx bytes as
preceded that event in the recording. Without this gating a replay would
deliver responses before the SDK even sends the requests.

`strictTx` additionally asserts the written bytes match the recorded tx
stream byte-for-byte (protocol regression mode). `realtime` paces rx
events by their recorded timestamps.

### stackTraceLimit

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `targetObject` | `object` |
| `constructorOpt?` | `Function` |

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

[`DepzError`](#class-depzerror).[`captureStackTrace`](#capturestacktrace-3)

# Class: Stream\<T\>

Defined in: [stream.ts:123](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/stream.ts#L123)

The subscribers, the pull queues and the counters of one kind of item
(contract 07 §3): `dev.measurements`, `dev.frames`, `dev.samples`,
`dev.reports`, `dev.events`.

Consumer side: `on(cb)` subscribes a callback (read-pump context — do not
block), `subscribe(maxsize)` makes an eager bounded drop-oldest iterator,
`next(timeoutMs)` waits for one item and is released by the device's
`close()`, `droppedCounts` and `parseErrors` are its counters. Owner side
(the sensor class, not public): the read pump emits one item per decoded
report and bumps `parseErrors` for a report it could not decode.
Subscribers are held as copy-on-write arrays: the pump iterates the array
it started with while callers replace the field — nothing is mutated under
the pump.

## Type Parameters

| Type Parameter |
| ------ |
| `T` |

### subscribe()

```ts
subscribe(maxsize?, opts?): StreamIterator<T>;
```

Defined in: [stream.ts:176](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/stream.ts#L176)

Async iterator over the items — bounded, drop-oldest (`droppedCount` on
the iterator); `maxsize` defaults to the stream's. Subscribes at the
call — items emitted after it are never missed — and ends when the
device closes or the consumer breaks out of iteration. The end is quiet
(`done: true`) after the program's own `close()` and after a loss alike;
the device's `lost` tells them apart (contract 07 §3).

| Parameter | Type |

### next()

```ts
next(timeoutMs?): Promise<T>;
```

Defined in: [stream.ts:200](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/stream.ts#L200)

Wait for the next item on a one-slot queue of its own, subscribed for
this call only.

Rejects with `DepzTimeoutError(what, timeoutMs)` when nothing arrives in
time. As soon as the device ends — before the call, or while waiting (an
item already queued still wins) — rejects with `LinkClosedError` after the
program's own `close()` and `DeviceLostError` (carrying the cause) after a
loss (contract 07 §3).
`timeoutMs` is a number ≥ 0, `Infinity` for no timeout (the wait ends
with the item or the close); a negative or NaN one is a RangeError. The
`events` stream offers no `next` (contract 07 §3: no single report to
name): there the call is refused with `InvalidStateError`.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default value |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `2000` |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`T`\>

## Properties

### stackTraceLimit

```ts
static stackTraceLimit: number;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `targetObject` | `object` |
| `constructorOpt?` | `Function` |

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

[`DepzError`](#class-depzerror).[`captureStackTrace`](#capturestacktrace-3)

### events

```ts

```

Defined in: [device/device.ts:187](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/device/device.ts#L187)

The unsolicited / diagnostic events of the device (contract 07 §2):
`events.on(cb)` subscribes (read-pump context; do not block),
`events.subscribe()` iterates. There is no `events.next()` — no single
report to wait for (§3).

The streamed measurements (contract 07 §3): `on(cb)` subscribes,
`subscribe(maxsize)` iterates, `next(timeoutMs)` waits for one;
`droppedCounts` and `parseErrors` (stream reports the driver could not
decode, or shorter than their header — counted before `init()` too) are
its counters.

### requireOpen()

```ts
protected requireOpen(): void;
```

Defined in: [device/device.ts:477](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/device/device.ts#L477)

Throws what every request of a handed-over, lost or closed device throws (contract 07 §3): lost
(whatever came after it), or closed by this side. A sensor class calls it before a guard of its
own state — "stop the stream first" — so that a board unplugged while it streamed says it is
lost, not that it still streams.

`void`

# Class: Vl53l4cd

Defined in: [sensors/vl53l4/vl53l4.ts:98](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/vl53l4/vl53l4.ts#L98)

VL53L4CD single-zone ToF device.

`init()` runs the ULD boot sequence (no firmware blob — the sensor carries
its own), then configure and `startRanging()`. Configuration methods must
not be called while ranging: the INT-driven stream owns the register bank
(contract 10). `measurements` is the stream (contract 07 §3).

### stackTraceLimit

```ts
static stackTraceLimit: number;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `targetObject` | `object` |
| `constructorOpt?` | `Function` |

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

```ts
Error.captureStackTrace
```

# Class: Vl53l7ch

Defined in: [sensors/vl53l7/vl53l7.ts:156](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/vl53l7/vl53l7.ts#L156)

VL53L7CH ToF device: the VL53L7CX superset. `init()` downloads the CH
firmware blob (VL53LMZ ULD 2.0.16, the same blob as VL53L8CH) and adds

stream in chunks (≤ 8192 B total).

# Class: Vl53l7cx

Defined in: [sensors/vl53l7/vl53l7.ts:52](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/vl53l7/vl53l7.ts#L52)

VL53L7CX ToF device (8×8 zones, 90° field of view). `init()` downloads the
~84 KB L5/L7 sensor firmware (~1.4 s at the board's default 1 MHz I2C),
then configure and `startRanging()` exactly as on `Vl53l8cx`.

Base class of the I2C family: `Vl53l5cx` (same blob, MZ module) and
`Vl53l7ch` (CH blob, adds CNH) inherit it.

# Class: Vl53l8ch

Defined in: [sensors/vl53l8/vl53l8.ts:539](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/vl53l8/vl53l8.ts#L539)

VL53L8CH device: the VL53L8CX superset. Inherits every CX method and adds
Compact-Network-Histogram (CNH) output. `init()` downloads the CH firmware
blob (VL53LMZ ULD 2.0.16). CNH is the reason to run CH firmware: each frame
can additionally carry a per-aggregate distance histogram.

# Class: Vl53l8cx

Defined in: [sensors/vl53l8/vl53l8.ts:121](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/vl53l8/vl53l8.ts#L121)

VL53L8CX ToF device: `init()` downloads the ~84 KB sensor firmware (takes a
few seconds over CDC), then configure and `startRanging()`.

This is the base class for both silicon variants. The VL53L8CH superset
(compact-network-histogram output) lives in `Vl53l8ch`, which inherits every
method here. All configuration methods require `init()` first and must not
be called while ranging (the ULD talks to the current register bank; the
stream owns it — contract 04).

- [`DepzDevice`](#class-depzdevice)

### stackTraceLimit

```ts
static stackTraceLimit: number;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `targetObject` | `object` |
| `constructorOpt?` | `Function` |

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

```ts
Error.captureStackTrace
```

# Class: Vl53lx

Defined in: [sensors/vl53lx/vl53lx.ts:208](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/vl53lx/vl53lx.ts#L208)

A board of the VL53L 1D family (firmware `APP_VL53L0_4`).

`init()` binds the (product, driver kind) pair and runs the ULD's
sensorInit; `configure()` re-initialises and applies the ranging
configuration — call it before every run. Then `startRanging()` arms the MCU
stream and measurements arrive on `measurements` (contract 07 §3).
Configuration must not change while ranging.

This generic class serves any product (read from the board's device name,
or `product` at init); the per-product subclasses (`Vl53l0x`...) fix it.

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

```ts
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;
```

Defined in: ../node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `targetObject` | `object` |
| `constructorOpt?` | `Function` |

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

[`DepzError`](#class-depzerror).[`captureStackTrace`](#capturestacktrace-3)

# Class: WsBackendTransport

Defined in: [transport/ws-backend.ts:107](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/transport/ws-backend.ts#L107)

How the SDK calls a transport (contract 07 §3, "The host-supplied link") —
what a transport given to `openOnTransport` or a device constructor has to
cope with. Everything runs on the event loop: there are no threads and no
read slices.

- `open` is called once, on a transport not yet open; `readable` once, after
  it, and that iterator is the only reader for the whole connection.
- `write` is called once per frame, a whole frame per call, in frame order
  and **without waiting for the previous `write`**: unlike the other SDKs,
  this one does not serialize writes, so a transport keeps them in order
  itself. It resolves when everything is written and rejects otherwise, and
  it must settle within a bounded time: a request waits for its `write`, so
  one that never settles never ends, not even at its timeout.
- `close` is called by every `DepzDevice.close()` and when the read fails
  (then again by the program's own `close()`): it must be idempotent. It
  may come during a pending read or `write`, and it must end the `readable`
  iterator; the device does not wait for that iterator.
- `onDisconnect` is subscribed once, when the read starts.
- A loss, unless the program is closing the device: `readable` throwing
  (logged with `console.error`, kept as the `cause`; the SDK closes the
  transport), `readable` ending, or the `onDisconnect` callback (no cause;
  the SDK does not call `close` until the program does). The device closes
  and every later request fails with `DeviceLostError`.
- A rejected `write` fails only that request, as a `DepzError` as it is and
  as `DeviceLostError` otherwise (`LinkClosedError` while closing), the
  rejection as its `cause`; the device ends when the read reports the loss.
- A rejected `close` reaches the program from its own `close()` (the device
  still ends); after a failed read it is dropped.

# Enumeration: ExecutableCommand

Defined in: [sensors/bno086/shtp.ts:45](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/sensors/bno086/shtp.ts#L45)

One-byte host writes on the executable channel (SHTP channel 1). The hub
answers none of them. `Reset` restarts the hub (answered later by the 0x01
reset-complete on the same channel); `Sleep` stops every report except those
enabled with `FeatureFlag.Wakeup | FeatureFlag.AlwaysOn`, keeping the
configuration; `On` ends `Sleep` and every report resumes at its rate.

Set Feature `flags` bits (SH-2 §6.5.4) for `Bno086.enable({ flags })`.

`Wakeup | AlwaysOn` keeps a sensor reporting through `Bno086.sleep()`: on a
DEPZ BNO086 (SH-2 3.12.6, 2026-10-16) such a report kept its full rate
during sleep, delivered on SHTP channel 4 (wake input), while every other
report stopped.

Defined in: [discovery.ts:417](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/discovery.ts#L417)

Continue the open base device `dev` as `className` on the same connection
(contract 02 §4.4): no reopen — the transport, the read pump and the host
packet sequence numbers run on. `dev` must be a plain `DepzDevice` with
nothing in flight and no stream open; it is spent afterwards (its
`close()` is a no-op, requests on it fail) — use the returned object.
`"device"` returns `dev` itself; `"bootloader"` throws `BootloaderModeError`.

`classOptions` go to the class constructor (e.g. a BNO086 / VL53Lx option);
the request timeout defaults to `dev.timeoutMs`.

# Function: openDeviceByDeviceSerial()

```ts
function openDeviceByDeviceSerial(
   ports, 
   factory, 
   target?, 
opts?): Promise<DepzDevice>;
```

Defined in: [discovery.ts:593](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/discovery.ts#L593)

Select and open a device by its DEVICE-reported serial (GET_SERIAL), for
transports that cannot enumerate USB iSerials (WebSerial). Probes every
given port (open → GET_SERIAL → close), orders the answers by device
serial, then selects — `opts.serial` picks an exact match, a numeric
`target` picks the Nth, otherwise the smallest serial — and reopens it.

The probing cost (opening each granted port once) is the price of not
having USB iSerials up front; the *result* matches Node's serial-based
selection because for programmed units USB iSerial == device serial.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `ports` | [`DepzPortInfo`](#interface-depzportinfo)[] |
| `factory` | [`TransportFactory`](#type-alias-transportfactory) |
| `target?` | `number` \| `null` |
| `opts?` | [`OpenDeviceOptions`](#interface-opendeviceoptions) |

## Returns

`Promise`\<[`DepzDevice`](#class-depzdevice)\>

# Function: openDeviceFrom()

```ts
function openDeviceFrom(
   ports, 
   factory, 
   target?, 
opts?): Promise<DepzDevice>;
```

Defined in: [discovery.ts:518](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/discovery.ts#L518)

Open the right sensor class for `target` (contract 02 §4).

- `undefined`/`null`: the candidate with the alphabetically-smallest USB
  iSerial (or the one whose serial == `opts.serial`). No candidate → throws
  `NoDepzDeviceError` (never falls back to "first port in system").
- `number N`: the Nth candidate, sorted by USB iSerial (0-based). Out of
  range → `NoDepzDeviceError`.
- `string`: open exactly that port path; warns if its (vid,pid) is not a
  known DEPZ id (may be an unprogrammed unit).
- `DeviceInfo`: opens its `.port`.

| ------ | ------ |
| `ports` | [`DepzPortInfo`](#interface-depzportinfo)[] |
| `factory` | [`TransportFactory`](#type-alias-transportfactory) |
| `target?` | [`OpenTarget`](#type-alias-opentarget) |
| `opts?` | [`OpenDeviceOptions`](#interface-opendeviceoptions) |

`Promise`\<[`DepzDevice`](#class-depzdevice)\>

# Function: openOnTransport()

```ts
function openOnTransport(transport, opts?): Promise<DepzDevice>;
```

Defined in: [discovery.ts:456](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/discovery.ts#L456)

Open a device on a connection that cannot be reopened — a replay or
recording transport, an adopted port (contract 02 §4.4). Opens
`transport` (not yet open, as for any `DepzDevice`), runs the same probe as
`probePort` on it (GET_NAME_ACTIVE_SOFTWARE, GET_DEVICE_NAME, GET_SERIAL),
resolves the class with `resolveSensorClass` from the answers and the
given USB id, and continues as that class on the same connection
(`attachSensorClass`). On failure the transport is closed. No answer to
GET_NAME_ACTIVE_SOFTWARE → `NoDepzDeviceError`, as is a transport that
could not be opened (its error as the `cause`, contract 07 §3); a
bootloader → `BootloaderModeError`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type |

| `transport` | [`SerialTransport`](#interface-serialtransport) |
| `opts` | [`OpenOnTransportOptions`](#interface-openontransportoptions) |

## Returns

`Promise`\<[`DepzDevice`](#class-depzdevice)\>

```ts
  | "vl53l8cx"
  | "device";
```

Defined in: [discovery.ts:365](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/discovery.ts#L365)

The canonical class name for a device's probe answers and its port's USB
(vid, pid) — contract 02 §4.4, pure; the reference every SDK matches.

`softwareName` is the GET_NAME_ACTIVE_SOFTWARE answer, `deviceName` the
GET_DEVICE_NAME answer ("" when there was none); the USB id is
null/undefined when unknown (a replay, a bridge).

- `BOOTDEPZ_*` → "bootloader".
- `vl53l8` → "vl53l8ch" if the USB model is VL53L8CH, else "vl53l8cx".
- `vl53l7` → the USB model if VL53L5CX / L7CX / L7CH, else the model
  stamped in the device name, else "vl53l7cx" (contract 11 §1).
- `vl53lx` → the USB model if one of the six 1D products, else the product
  stamped in the device name, else generic; VL53L4CD (no class of its own
  on that firmware) and no product → "vl53lx" (contract 12 §1).
- any other known token → its class; unknown `APP_*` (or a name that is
  neither APP_ nor BOOTDEPZ) → "device".

Pinned by the probe golden vectors shared by all DEPZ SDKs.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `softwareName` | `string` |
| `deviceName` | `string` \| `null` \| `undefined` |
| `usbVid` | `number` \| `null` \| `undefined` |
| `usbPid` | `number` \| `null` \| `undefined` |

## Returns

  \| `"sr04"`
  \| `"vl53lx"`
  \| `"bno086"`
  \| `"bno055"`
  \| `"tmf8829"`
  \| `"bootloader"`
  \| `"vl53l8ch"`
  \| `"vl53l0x"`

  \| `"vl53l5cx"`
  \| `"vl53l7cx"`
  \| `"vl53l7ch"`
  \| `"vl53l8cx"`
  \| `"device"`

# Function: resolveVl53l7Model()

```ts
function resolveVl53l7Model(usbModel, deviceName): Vl53l7Model;
```

Defined in: [protocol/vl53l7.ts:153](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/protocol/vl53l7.ts#L153)

Pick the L5/L7 class (contract 11 §1). All three boards run APP_VL53L7 and
the silicon only tells L5 from L7 after init() (module_type), never CX from
CH — so the production USB PID model decides, then the device name the
bootloader was stamped with (`… VL53L7CH USB v2.1 …`), then the CX base
(safe: its blob runs on every L5/L7 part).

# Interface: Bno055Info

Defined in: [protocol/bno055.ts:129](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/protocol/bno055.ts#L129)

RPT_BNO_INFO — sensor identity (registers 0x00..0x06) plus bridge
diagnostics. Counters wrap silently; `i2cErrors` is cleared by every
successful reset handshake, the read timings and `slotsSkipped` at
START_STREAM. A rising
`sensorResets` means the bridge pulsed nRESET to recover the bus: the
sensor is back in CONFIG mode and the host must restore its configuration.

# Interface: SerialTransport

Defined in: [transport/types.ts:44](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/transport/types.ts#L44)

How the SDK calls a transport (contract 07 §3, "The host-supplied link") —
what a transport given to `openOnTransport` or a device constructor has to
cope with. Everything runs on the event loop: there are no threads and no
read slices.

- `open` is called once, on a transport not yet open; `readable` once, after
  it, and that iterator is the only reader for the whole connection.
- `write` is called once per frame, a whole frame per call, in frame order
  and **without waiting for the previous `write`**: unlike the other SDKs,
  this one does not serialize writes, so a transport keeps them in order
  itself. It resolves when everything is written and rejects otherwise, and
  it must settle within a bounded time: a request waits for its `write`, so
  one that never settles never ends, not even at its timeout.
- `close` is called by every `DepzDevice.close()` and when the read fails
  (then again by the program's own `close()`): it must be idempotent. It
  may come during a pending read or `write`, and it must end the `readable`
  iterator; the device does not wait for that iterator.
- `onDisconnect` is subscribed once, when the read starts.
- A loss, unless the program is closing the device: `readable` throwing
  (logged with `console.error`, kept as the `cause`; the SDK closes the
  transport), `readable` ending, or the `onDisconnect` callback (no cause;
  the SDK does not call `close` until the program does). The device closes
  and every later request fails with `DeviceLostError`.
- A rejected `write` fails only that request, as a `DepzError` as it is and
  as `DeviceLostError` otherwise (`LinkClosedError` while closing), the
  rejection as its `cause`; the device ends when the read reports the loss.
- A rejected `close` reaches the program from its own `close()` (the device
  still ends); after a failed read it is dropped.

`Vl53l8cx.frames.subscribe()`, `Bno086.reports.subscribe()` … return: a
bounded, drop-oldest async iterator (contract 07 §3). `for await` it, or
call `next()`; leaving the loop (`break`, `return()`) unsubscribes from the
device.

# Interface: Tmf8829PixelResults

Decoded results of one frame or of a merged measurement. Per-peak arrays
are flat `[peak][row][col]` (row-major); noise / xtalk `[row][col]`. Raw
sensor integers: distance in 0.25 mm (or mm with the footer flag), not yet
clock-corrected. Absent fields are null.

# Interface: Vl53lxInfo

Defined in: [protocol/vl53lx.ts:91](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/protocol/vl53lx.ts#L91)

RPT_VL53_INFO (v2.00, 23 bytes) — bridge state only; the bridge reads no
sensor register. Counters are free-running (wrap silently): watch
increments. `slotsSkipped` = a slot that never got the bus, `i2cErrors` =
a bus that answered badly (since power-up, the last XSHUT reset or
VL53_CLEAR_I2C_ERRORS — the SDK sends that at the end of every sensor init,
so the NACKs of a resetting die are not counted), `framesDropped` = a good
sample the USB TX ring had no room for (since the stream was armed).

[`WebSocketLike`](#interface-websocketlike)

***

### openTimeoutMs?

```ts
optional openTimeoutMs?: number;
```

Defined in: [transport/ws-backend.ts:97](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/transport/ws-backend.ts#L97)

Ceiling on `open()` (ms, default DEFAULT\_OPEN\_TIMEOUT\_MS).

The socket opening is not the same event as the *port* opening: the
backend accepts the WebSocket first, then opens the serial port in a
thread and only then sends `{"opened":true}`. If that open never returns
(a wedged adapter, a port held by something that never lets go), nothing
fires `onerror` or `onclose` and `open()` would await forever — taking the
caller's connect guard with it, which in the viewer leaves "Scan for
sensors" disabled with no way back but a reload. Pass `0` (or
`Infinity`) to disable; a negative or NaN value is a RangeError.

Every name `resolveSensorClass` returns: the canonical sensor classes of
contract 07 §1, `"vl53lx"` (the generic 1D-family class: an unstamped
board, or a VL53L4CD on the APP_VL53L0_4 firmware), `"tmf8829"`,
`"device"` (the base `DepzDevice`: an unknown application, or a name that
is neither APP_ nor BOOTDEPZ) and `"bootloader"` (no sensor class: use the
contract 06 client). BNO085 boards run APP_BNO086 and resolve to `"bno086"`.

# Class: NodeSerialTransport

Defined in: [transport/node.ts:77](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/transport/node.ts#L77)

How the SDK calls a transport (contract 07 §3, "The host-supplied link") —
what a transport given to `openOnTransport` or a device constructor has to
cope with. Everything runs on the event loop: there are no threads and no
read slices.

- `open` is called once, on a transport not yet open; `readable` once, after
  it, and that iterator is the only reader for the whole connection.
- `write` is called once per frame, a whole frame per call, in frame order
  and **without waiting for the previous `write`**: unlike the other SDKs,
  this one does not serialize writes, so a transport keeps them in order
  itself. It resolves when everything is written and rejects otherwise, and
  it must settle within a bounded time: a request waits for its `write`, so
  one that never settles never ends, not even at its timeout.
- `close` is called by every `DepzDevice.close()` and when the read fails
  (then again by the program's own `close()`): it must be idempotent. It
  may come during a pending read or `write`, and it must end the `readable`
  iterator; the device does not wait for that iterator.
- `onDisconnect` is subscribed once, when the read starts.
- A loss, unless the program is closing the device: `readable` throwing
  (logged with `console.error`, kept as the `cause`; the SDK closes the
  transport), `readable` ending, or the `onDisconnect` callback (no cause;
  the SDK does not call `close` until the program does). The device closes
  and every later request fails with `DeviceLostError`.
- A rejected `write` fails only that request, as a `DepzError` as it is and
  as `DeviceLostError` otherwise (`LinkClosedError` while closing), the
  rejection as its `cause`; the device ends when the read reports the loss.
- A rejected `close` reaches the program from its own `close()` (the device
  still ends); after a failed read it is dropped.

Enumerate DEPZ devices on the system's serial ports (Node only).

With `matchUsb` (default) only ports carrying a known DEPZ (vid,pid) are
probed — fast, and it never pokes unrelated ports. Set `matchUsb: false`
for a legacy probe-everything scan.

# Function: openDevice()


Defined in: [transport/node.ts:226](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/transport/node.ts#L226)

Open the right sensor class for `target` over `serialport` (Node only).

`target` is a port path (string, under any alias of the enumerated port:
`/dev/serial/by-id/…`), a candidate index (number, sorted by USB iSerial),
a `DeviceInfo` from `listDepzDevices()`, or omitted for the lowest-serial
candidate. Throws `NoDepzDeviceError` when nothing matches — it never
grabs an arbitrary system port. See [openDeviceFrom](#function-opendevicefrom).

Withdraw the page's permission for a granted port, so it is no longer listed
by `getGrantedPorts()` / `getGrantedWebUsbPorts()` and needs the chooser
again. The port must be closed first. Resolves to false, changing nothing,

```ts
function listDepzDevices(opts?): Promise<DeviceInfo[]>;
```

Defined in: [transport/webserial.ts:243](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/transport/webserial.ts#L243)

Probe the already-granted WebSerial ports and return the DEPZ devices among
them, ordered by DEVICE serial (GET_SERIAL) — the USB iSerial is unavailable
in the browser, so the serial is read over the protocol. By default every
granted port is probed (`matchUsb: false`) since a granted port is
user-curated; pass `matchUsb: true` to probe only known-DEPZ vid/pids.

`Promise`\<[`DeviceInfo`](#interface-deviceinfo)[]\>

# Function: openDevice()

```ts
function openDevice(target?, opts?): Promise<DepzDevice>;
```

Defined in: [transport/webserial.ts:264](https://github.com/depz-ai/depz-sensor-sdk/blob/main/packages/depz-sensor-sdk-ts/src/transport/webserial.ts#L264)

Open the right sensor class for a granted WebSerial port.

`target` is a `WebSerialPortLike` (typically fresh from
`navigator.serial.requestPort()`), a granted-port path string / `DeviceInfo`
from `listDepzDevices()`, a candidate index (number, ordered by device
serial), or omitted for the smallest-serial DEPZ candidate. `opts.serial`
selects the candidate whose device serial matches exactly. Selection probes
the granted ports; explicit targets open directly. Throws
`NoDepzDeviceError` when nothing matches.
